spike_plan.kill_if: Median ratio at or below 1.05, a repeat-to-repeat spread above about 15%, any answer disagreement, or the build cannot be made offline. Also kill if per-file licences forbid shipping the QF_BV subset.
spike_plan.pass_if: Later tag median ratio is at least 1.2 over the older tag across the three repeats, spread under about 10%, zero status disagreements, and the build runs offline after vendoring.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone bitwuzla at the older snapshot tag (e.g. 0.8.2) and at 0.9.1 (no need for history beyond the tag).
Build both with meson; record which SAT backend and dependency downloads the build needs. Note any network fetch at build time.
Download QF_BV.tar.zst from Zenodo and draw a fixed random sample of about 150 instances, seeded, spanning families.
Check each file's set-info :license and record the licence per file.
Run both binaries serially with a 60 s timeout on the same machine, three repeats each. Record time, result, and PAR-2.
Compare answers to set-info :status and across binaries. Any disagreement is a wrong-answer event.
Compute the median per-instance time ratio and PAR-2 for each repeat, and the run-to-run spread.

v1.summary: The seed's real base holds up: Bitwuzla is MIT, the SMT-LIB 2025 QF_BV set is an official Zenodo record, and the upstream later tag exists. The open risks are an unmeasured reference speedup, a public later tag that the snapshot must hide, per-file benchmark licences, and an offline build that needs a vendored SAT solver, so the spike must confirm a meaningful median speedup before any build.

v2.note: The Bitwuzla MIT licence and the SMT-LIB 2025 Zenodo record are confirmed. The core reference facts were not found: no measured QF_BV speedup between any two tags, no diff size, and no pick of a base tag backed by a perf changelog. The release pair is arbitrary and may give a ratio near 1. SAT-backed runtimes are chaotic, so small heuristic changes swing instances by orders of magnitude, and a median ratio under gVisor timing noise risks K4. Switching the SAT backend or settings may be a dominant single lever. Per-file benchmark licences were not checked. Revive only as a release pair whose changelog shows a measured QF_BV gain.
